events.title: The martyrdom of Blessed Miguel Pro
events.shortBlurb: A young Mexican Jesuit was shot by a firing squad, crying out his love for Christ the King…
body: Miguel Agustín Pro, born at Guadalupe in Zacatecas on 13 January 1891, entered the Jesuits in 1911 and, driven into exile by the persecution, was ordained at Enghien in Belgium in 1925. He returned to Mexico in 1926, when the laws of President Calles had silenced the churches, and ministered in secret to the faithful of Mexico City, bringing them the sacraments in disguise.

In November 1927 an attempt was made on the life of the former president Obregón by men who used a car once owned by the Pro family; Miguel and his brothers were arrested, and without trial Calles ordered him shot. He was executed on 23 November 1927 together with his brother Humberto, the government having commanded that the execution be photographed and the pictures published.

Refusing the blindfold, Pro forgave the firing squad, stretched out his arms in the form of a cross with a crucifix in one hand and a rosary in the other, and died crying 'Viva Cristo Rey' — Long live Christ the King. The photographs, published to terrorize, spread his fame instead. John Paul II beatified him on 25 September 1988, among the martyrs of the Mexican persecution.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Beatification of Blessed Miguel Agustín Pro (vatican.va)
